- When sentiment is negative and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the forecast peak by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If forecast consistently overshoots true values in the first 5–7 days after a spike, apply a downward correction of 2–5% per day to align with mean reversion.  
- When sentiment is positive and forecast is low, avoid underestimating the next 3–5 days — increase forecast by 2–4% to capture sentiment-driven momentum.  
- If true outcome is consistently higher than forecast in the last 3–5 days of the 30-day window, adjust future forecasts upward by 1–3% to reflect recent trend persistence.  
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed, avoid overfitting to recent volatility — use a smoother trend filter to prevent erratic forecast swings.
